summary: Skagit County tower framed and erected in 1946 for the state Forestry Division, removed in 1970; the summit is now a fenced communication site.

facts.design: 40-foot ring-connected treated timber tower with L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Removed in 1970; a large communication tower and a fenced area now stand on the site (Willhite)

staffing.status: One June 1960 newspaper item names a Forest Service lookout on 'Mt. Fairley'; not confirmed as this tower; no other staffing found

access.note: Route runs on DNR land past a gate; the summit is a fenced communication site, and no source says whether the public may enter the fenced area

visit.trail_note: Willhite: walk or bike the road 2.7 miles to its end, then an ATV track through a clear-cut to the communication tower. A January 2026 visitor's blog describes a road walk with a short climb to the old lookout site.

events.note: Built 1946 as a 40-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab (FFLOS, firelookout.com); the 1946 annual report of the Forestry Division, as quoted by Forest Lookouts and Willhite, says it was framed in the shop and erected on the mountain
June 9, 1960 Arlington Times item says Helen Fosnaugh took up a post in the tower on 'Mt. Fairley' with the U.S. Forest Service; it conflicts with the state credit and the peak spelling differs
Registered March 26, 2012 as US 1242, WA 142; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The June 1960 item says the U.S. Forest Service ran the post and spells the peak 'Mt. Fairley'. FFLOS and firelookout.com credit the state Washington Division of Forestry/DNR. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Brief record confirmed: gone, 40 ft (12.2 m), state Division of Forestry/DNR, FFLOS registration 2012. No fire history found in the five sources read or in one search. Staffing rests on one 1960 item that conflicts with the state credit and spells the peak differently; recorded as staffed but the story does not link it firmly to this tower. Today's condition rests on Willhite's page and one personal January 2026 blog post. The access level 'restricted' is an editorial reading of the fenced communication site, not a stated rule. Access was 'unknown' in the brief.
